Now jump ahead a few days.
Back in the city, the streets are dark and white with frost.
Windows still glow, powered by fuel burning in the dark.
Above the towers, the sky is full of stars, day and night.
The temperature would drop below zero, and keep going.
The palm trees would be the first to give up.
They were never made for frost.
Their leaves would turn brittle and dark.
Frost would creep up the walls, floor by floor.
Minus ten.
Car engines would struggle to start.
One by one, the cars would stop where they stand.
Inside the walls, pipes would freeze and burst.
The city would grow quieter every day.
Snow on the roads would never melt.
Not even by day, because there is no day.
Only the street lamps would still burn, over empty sidewalks.
Every heater in the city would be running at once.
The power grid was never built for a night that never ends.
By the end of the first week, the average temperature on Earth would be about minus seventeen degrees.
And then, the power fails.
In the dark, it would be colder than almost any winter most of us have ever known.
And not just here.
Everywhere on Earth, at the same time.
And it would only be the beginning.
